header.title: BCF Manager Studio
header.heroAlt: Dashboard of a fictitious residential building with the number of open, ongoing and closed issues, a bar chart per priority and issue cards with snapshots from the model
header.label: BIM collaboration
header.tagline: All BIM issues of a project in one place, on your own server
header.desc: BCF Manager Studio is a concept for issue management in BIM projects. You collect the findings from model checks per project, discuss them with your team and pass them on as a BCF file to any other BIM software.

meta.description: Concept for open-source issue management in BIM projects: BCF 2.1 issues per project, with snapshots, comments, a dashboard, .bcfzip import and export and the BCF API 2.1. On your own server with Docker.
meta.title: BCF Manager Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

issues.alt: Project overview with three fictitious projects, each with an image from the model, location and short description
issues.title: Every project its own issue list
issues.desc: Create one place per project for all findings, with a name, location, description and a project image. The overview shows at a glance which building it is, and nobody has to search through loose e-mails and spreadsheets any more.

list.alt: Issue list of a fictitious residential building with seven issues, each with status, priority, type and date
list.title: See in one list what is still open
list.desc: Every issue is listed with its status, priority and type, such as clash, issue or remark. The dashboard counts the open, ongoing and closed issues and shows per priority where the work is.

model.alt: Issue about a roof element with the snapshot from the model at the top, the element concerned highlighted in blue
model.title: See right away where the problem is
model.desc: Every issue shows the snapshot from the model, with the camera position. The viewpoint refers to the elements by their IFC GlobalId, so a BCF viewer jumps straight to the right part.

team.alt: Issue with the description, a series of comments and on the right the details: status, priority, stage, assigned to, deadline and labels
team.title: Discuss the issue where it belongs
team.desc: Comments sit on the issue itself, with date and time, so the whole discussion stays together. Next to them you see who it is assigned to, the deadline, the stage and the labels.

notice.text: Concept: there is no version to install yet, and the online trial version was shut down on 8 October 2026. The screenshots come from a local test setup with fictitious projects.

projects.title: Create projects
projects.desc: With a name, location and description, and a project image of your own.

newissue.title: New issue
newissue.desc: Title, description, type, status and priority in one form.

status.title: Status and priority
status.desc: Open, active, closed or reopened; from low to critical, as BCF defines them.

dashboard.title: Dashboard per project

filters.title: Filtering
filters.desc: Show only the issues with a given status or priority on the dashboard.

snapshots.title: Snapshots on every issue
snapshots.desc: The image from the model is shown large on the issue and small on the dashboard cards.

camera.title: Camera position
camera.desc: Perspective or orthographic, with the camera position as stored in the viewpoint.

globalid.title: Elements by IFC GlobalId
globalid.desc: Selection, visibility and colouring per element, so a viewer shows the right part.

comments.title: Comments
comments.desc: Write a comment on the issue; every comment gets a date and time.

details.title: Assignment and deadline
details.desc: Who the issue is assigned to, the deadline, the stage and the labels, as they come from the BCF file.

members.title: Members per project
members.desc: Add colleagues to a project as owner, administrator, member or viewer.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.desc: Your team signs in with the organisation's existing account.

import.title: Import BCF files
import.desc: Read in a .bcfzip with all issues, comments and viewpoints, for example from a model check.

export.title: Export BCF files
export.desc: Download all issues of a project as a .bcfzip for any BCF software.

api.title: BCF API 2.1
api.desc: The open standard API for projects, issues, comments and viewpoints, for links with other software.

apikeys.title: API keys per project
apikeys.desc: Give a script or checking tool access to one project, optionally with an expiry date.

nextcloud.title: Save to your Nextcloud
nextcloud.desc: Keep the issues as a .bcfzip in the project folder, next to the IFC models, and open them from there again.

manifest.title: Project manifest kept up to date

selfhosted.title: On your own server

tenants.title: Several organisations

ribbon.title: Familiar ribbon
ribbon.desc: The same ribbon as the other OpenAEC apps, with shortcuts for import (Ctrl+I) and export (Ctrl+E).

features.label: Features
features.heading: From finding to fix, with the whole team
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

api.title: Full BCF API 2.1
api.desc: Versions, project extensions and the selection, visibility and colouring of viewpoints too.

cloud.title: Save to Nextcloud
cloud.desc: From the File menu you save the issues to the project folder, or open them from there.

manifest.title: Project manifest

tenants.title: Several organisations
tenants.desc: One installation for several organisations, each with its own Nextcloud.

login.title: Shared sign-in server

whatsnew.label: New in April 2026
whatsnew.title: The full BCF API, saving to your cloud
whatsnew.desc: The latest new features date from April 2026. Development has been paused since then; there is no release yet.

files.a: BCF files (.bcfzip) in version 2.1, as written by Solibri, Navisworks, BIMcollab, Revit and the OpenAEC apps. BCF 3.0 is not supported yet. BCF Manager Studio does not open the IFC model itself; use an IFC viewer for that.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: Yes, on a server. BCF Manager Studio is a server application that you put on your own server with Docker, together with PostgreSQL. Your team then simply works in the browser. There is no ready-made release yet, and the online trial version was shut down on 8 October 2026.

price.a: Nothing. The source code is public on GitHub and you only pay for your own server. There is no licence file with the source code yet; it will come with the first release.

format.q: In which file format is my work saved?
format.a: The issues are stored in a PostgreSQL database on your server, with the snapshots as images alongside. You can export them at any time as a .bcfzip, the open buildingSMART standard, or save them that way to your Nextcloud.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: The server runs in Docker, on Linux. Your team works in a modern browser on Windows, macOS or Linux.

practice.a: Yes. BCF is the open buildingSMART standard for BIM coordination: a model check produces issues, which you discuss, assign and close. Statuses, priorities, stages and labels follow BCF 2.1, so they stay intact when you exchange them with other parties.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: There is no MCP server yet. An assistant or script with an API key can, however, read and create issues, comments and viewpoints of a project through the BCF API 2.1.

ready.a: Not out of the box. BCF Manager Studio is a concept: there is no release and no public trial version any more, and development has been paused since April 2026. If you want, you can build it yourself from the source code on GitHub and put it on your own server.

edit.q: Can I edit an issue on screen?
edit.a: Partly. On screen you create issues and write comments. You cannot yet change the status, assignment and deadline of an existing issue on screen, but you can through a BCF import or the API. Searching the issue list is still to come as well.

revit.a: Through BCF files, yes: you simply read in a .bcfzip from Revit. There is also a separate test version of a Revit 2025 plug-in that opens .bcfzip files in Revit. A direct connection between that plug-in and BCF Manager Studio does not work yet.

oidc.title: OIDC · JWT · API keys
oidc.desc: Single sign-on through Authentik, JWT sessions and keys per project.

nextcloud.title: Nextcloud · WebDAV
nextcloud.desc: Storage in your own Nextcloud through the shared openaec-cloud library, with .wefc manifests.
